I must admit, we’ve been expecting to see a solid pickup in growth for quite a

The Fed cut short-term interest rates from six and a half percent to
one and three-quarters percent in 2001.

And we brought the rate down to 1 percent with additional cuts in
November 2002 and last June.

And that bodes well for the future, because faster productivity
growth creates business opportunities that stimulate economic
growth.

Real GDP grew by 3.3 percent in the second quarter and by a sizzling 8.2 percent

It was especially encouraging to see the performance of business
investment in equipment and software, where much of the sluggishness
over the past couple of years had been concentrated.
This sector showed very rapid gains.

This improvement in business investment has helped the beleaguered
manufacturing sector, which has finally begun to grow in recent months.

And, along with the rapid productivity growth, profit reports have been excellent
for the most part.

Now, we’ve thought for some time that the main downside risk to a robust economy was
the consumer.

two and a half years of sluggish growth.
